court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court at Bandra, Mumbai, F.C.A.NO.66 OF 2008 and F.C.A.NO.136 OF 2008
case_name: Kiran Hiralal Popat vs Suhasini @ Swati Kiran Popat
facts_of_case: The husband filed a petition for divorce on the ground of cruelty under Clause (ia) of Sub-section (1) of Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court dismissed the petition and directed the husband to pay maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: A party who obtains an ex parte decree fraudulently may have it set aside.
legal_principles.held: The learned Judge of the Family Court accepted the case of the wife that due to the settlement, the husband had assured the wife to withdraw the Petition. The learned Judge of the Family Court observed that the husband obtained the ex parte decree fraudulently.

legal_principles.principle: A settlement between parties can be a valid reason to set aside an ex parte decree.
legal_principles.held: The learned Judge of the Family Court accepted the case of the wife that due to the settlement, the husband had assured the wife to withdraw the Petition.

outcome.final_order: The final court order was that the appeal was allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court were set aside.
